title: Set service levels and quality targets (SLOs and non-functional requirements)
summary: How fast, reliable and secure a technical product must be is part of the requirement. Agree measurable targets before building, not after testing.

beginner: Learn the terms: a service level objective (SLO) is a reliability target, such as 99.9% of requests succeed.
Ask users what speed and reliability they need.
Agree two or three targets, such as response time and availability.
Make each target measurable and testable.
Add them to the acceptance criteria of the relevant work.
intermediate: Set SLOs from user needs, not from what the system does today.
Agree an error budget and what happens when it runs out.
Cover other qualities too, such as security and scalability.
experienced: Set SLO standards across services and teams.
Use error budgets to balance new features with reliability work.
Weigh the cost of each extra level of reliability.

canDelegateTo.task: Measure current reliability and set up monitoring
Advise on what targets are achievable

toolExamples.aws: Use monitoring dashboards to track SLOs.
toolExamples.gcp: Set up SLO monitoring for the service.
toolExamples.azure: Set alerts on availability and response time.

definitionOfDone: Two or three measurable targets agreed

leaderView.good: Speed, reliability and security targets are agreed, measurable and part of the requirement.
ask: What are our targets for speed and availability, and are we meeting them?
Who is told when we miss them?
signs: Non-functional requirements are added at the end.
Targets exist but no one measures them.
